answer.location_description: A full-width periodic horizontal banding pattern covering the whole image. It alternates in 2-row bands (period of 4 rows). The weights are strongest in rows 2-9 and 18-23 and act outside the central nodule region (rows ~10-13, cols ~9-14).
answer.shortcut_type: periodic horizontal stripe / scan-line banding artifact
answer.mechanism: There are two groups of structured layer-1 units. Group B (units 3, 8, 21, 24, 27, 28; negative biases) has row-constant positive weights on rows 0-1, 4-5, 8-9, 12-13 (edges), 16-17 and 20-21. It has negative weights on rows 2-3, 6-7 (right side), 14-15 (edges), 18-19 and 22-23. Group B feeds layer-2 units u1 (W2 +66 to +94), u8 (+91 to +93) and u10, which carry positive output weights (+99, +58, +46). So images with bright stripes in this phase push the logit toward malignant. Group A (units 2, 5, 14, 16, 17, 18, 19, 25, 29, 30; biases about +90) has the opposite-phase grating plus a small bright-centre detector. Group A feeds u9 and u11, which have negative output weights (-72, -64), and it inhibits u1 (-66 to -86). The net effect is a phase-sensitive horizontal grating detector that is independent of the nodule.
answer.evidence: Group B weights are uniform along whole rows, independent of column. Unit 3: row 2 is about -20 to -47 at every column, rows 4-5 about +25 to +43 at every column. Unit 24: rows 4-5 about +40, rows 8-9 about +45 to +65, rows 20-21 about +25 to +55, rows 2-3 about -25. Units 27 and 28 follow the same pattern. Group A shows the inverse. Unit 14: rows 2-3 about +40 to +60, rows 4-5 negative, rows 6-7 right side positive, rows 8-9 about -50, rows 14-15 left/right edges about +50, rows 18-19 about +30 to +60. Units 2, 5, 16, 19, 25, 29 and 30 are similar. Real, roughly isotropic lung tissue around a centred nodule gives no reason for full-width bands alternating every 2 rows. The pattern therefore indicates an acquisition or banding artifact correlated with the label.
answer.main_feature: Nodule size and density at the image centre. A small bright core with a dark surrounding ring (units 2, 5, 14, 25, 29, 30) drives benign. A larger bright region or annulus around the centre (units 3, 8, 24, 27, 28) and a broadly bright surround with a dark centre (unit 20) drive malignant.
